description:
verify.rs:784-806, 811-835, 872-899, 916-940: four byte-layout builders that differ only in the byte at index 1 (SIG_TYPE_CERTIFICATE_TIMESTAMP vs MERKLE_LEAF_TYPE_TIMESTAMPED_ENTRY) and the entry_type byte. They produce identical byte streams for v1/timestamped_entry/certificate_timestamp (all three constants are u8 value 0).

Suggested rewrite:
```rust
fn build_x509_entry(sct: &Sct, tag1: u8, cert_der: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>> { ... }
fn build_precert_entry(sct: &Sct, tag1: u8, issuer_key_hash: &[u8; 32], tbs: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>> { ... }
```
With public wrappers:
```rust
fn build_signed_input_x509_entry(sct, cert) = build_x509_entry(sct, SIG_TYPE_CERTIFICATE_TIMESTAMP, cert)
fn build_merkle_tree_leaf_x509_entry(sct, cert) = build_x509_entry(sct, MERKLE_LEAF_TYPE_TIMESTAMPED_ENTRY, cert)
```

Cuts 60 lines and makes the structural identity self-documenting. The existing comments at verify.rs:778-783 acknowledging the parallelism become unnecessary.

Counter-argument the author would offer (and which deserves engagement): keeping them separate makes the byte-layout for each RFC 6962 structure independently auditable. A reader auditing the precert_entry signed-input doesn't have to mentally trace through a helper to confirm the bytes. That has real value for security-sensitive code.

Net: weak preference for collapse, but not strong enough to block. Mark this 'opinion' if you agree the audit-friendly form wins.
title: build_signed_input_* and build_merkle_tree_leaf_* duplicate ~60 lines of byte-layout code
